issues.t: Burning oil and blue exhaust smoke
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, blue-gray smoke comes from the exhaust (especially after idling or on hard acceleration), and spark plugs may foul.
issues.why: The high-revving VTEC engine is known for burning oil as it ages, mostly from worn piston rings and valve stem seals. Owners of the 2001 report it as the top problem, at around 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and never let it run low. A compression and leak-down test will show whether rings or valve seals are to blame before you spend money.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks and damages the engine
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stops while driving and won't restart, sometimes after a slapping or ticking noise from the front of the engine.
issues.why: Prelude engines are interference designs, so when the timing belt snaps the pistons hit the valves. Owners report broken belts around 110,000 miles and major engine repairs.
issues.next: If there's no record of a timing belt change, have the belt, tensioner and water pump replaced now. Doing it now can prevent bent valves.

issues.t: Distributor wear causing misfires and power loss
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, hesitation, loss of power, and worse fuel economy, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Worn shaft bushings in the distributor let the rotor wobble, which upsets the spark timing and strength.
issues.next: Rule out spark plugs, wires, cap and rotor first, then have the distributor tested. A replacement distributor usually fixes it.

issues.t: Engine stalls or won't start from failed igniter
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or cranks but won't start, often when hot, with no spark.
issues.why: The ignition module (igniter) and coil sit inside the distributor and can fail with heat and age. When the igniter fails, spark stops completely.
issues.next: Have spark checked while the problem is happening. Because the igniter is built into the distributor, many shops replace the whole unit.

issues.t: Oil leak at the distributor
issues.sym: Oil wetting the end of the cylinder head and the distributor base, or a burning oil smell. If oil gets inside the distributor, misfires follow.
issues.why: The O-ring and shaft seal where the distributor plugs into the cylinder head harden and leak with age.
issues.next: Replace the O-ring early; it is a simple fix. If oil is inside the distributor cap, the internal seal is leaking and the distributor may need rebuilding.

issues.t: Warped front brake rotors
issues.sym: The steering wheel shakes or the brake pedal pulses when stopping, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: The front rotors on the Prelude are known to warp, which RepairPal lists among the model's common problems.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. They can sometimes be machined, but new rotors with new pads are usually the better fix.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints can wear and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, loose or wandering steering, and in the worst case a front wheel collapsing.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints can wear out early and pull apart.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 99V-069. If the recall was done long ago, still have the ball joints checked at every inspection on a car this old.

issues.t: Ignition switch can wear and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly cuts out while driving, sometimes with dash lights flickering.
issues.why: Contacts inside the ignition switch wear from high current and can briefly lose connection.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 02V-120 and have the switch replaced. Stalling in traffic is a crash risk.

issues.t: Key can be removed without the car in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out of the ignition even though the shifter is not in Park, so the car can roll away.
issues.why: The ignition interlock lever on automatic cars can fail to block the key.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 05V-025 and have the redesigned lever installed. Always set the parking brake.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Delayed or harsh shifts, slipping, flaring revs between gears, or the car not moving in Drive.
issues.why: Consumer Guide lists transmission failures on these years and notes Honda extended warranty coverage on some transmissions of this era. That coverage has ended.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and color. If it slips, avoid hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis; rebuilt or used units are the usual fix.

issues.t: ATTS warning light and system shutting off
issues.sym: The ATTS light comes on and the Type SH's torque-vectoring system turns itself off, so the car handles like a regular Prelude.
issues.why: The active torque transfer system's control unit could misread conditions and shut the system down. Honda released a revised control unit.
issues.next: Have the ATTS codes read and ask about the revised control unit. Check fluid in the ATTS unit as well.

issues.t: Check engine light from damaged transmission computer
issues.sym: Check engine light on automatic cars, sometimes with odd shifting.
issues.why: Electrical spikes from the ignition switch could damage the transmission control module.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the transmission computer is damaged, also make sure the ignition switch recall was done.

issues.t: Grinding when shifting into fifth gear
issues.sym: A grind or crunch when shifting from fourth into fifth on manual cars.
issues.why: A shift fork made out of specification could misalign fifth gear's synchro.
issues.next: Have the transmission inspected. The fix means opening the gearbox to replace the shift fork and possibly the synchro.

issues.t: Balance shaft oil plug can pop out
issues.sym: A sudden heavy oil leak, oil pressure light, and engine noise if driven on.
issues.why: A plug in the front balance shaft area could work loose, letting oil escape quickly and risking engine damage.
issues.next: Stop the engine at once if the oil light comes on. Have the plug area inspected and secured.

issues.t: Headliner rattling against rear window
issues.sym: A rattle or buzz from behind your head on rough roads.
issues.why: The rear corners of the headliner can rub the rear window.
issues.next: Have the headliner corners re-secured or padded.

issues.t: Buzzing heat shield near the ATTS unit
issues.sym: A buzz or rattle from under the car at certain speeds.
issues.why: A heat shield sits too close to the ATTS unit and can vibrate against it.
issues.next: Have the heat shield bent back or re-clamped.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle button can break
issues.sym: The buckle release button cracks and the buckle slides down to the floor.
issues.why: The button on the buckle could break with use.
issues.next: Have the buckle replaced so the belt latches and releases properly.

issues.t: Water leaking into rear footwells
issues.sym: Wet carpet or standing water in the rear footwells, often with a musty smell.
issues.why: Owners report water entering the rear seat and footwell area, which on this car commonly comes from blocked drains or tired body seals.
issues.next: Check sunroof drains, door seals and rear window seals. Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Sunroof surround leaks
issues.sym: Water stains on the headliner around the sunroof or drips after rain.
issues.why: Age and earlier crash repairs can let water in around the sunroof opening.
issues.next: Clean the sunroof drains and check the seal and headliner for water damage.

issues.t: Four-wheel steering (4WS) warning light
issues.sym: The 4WS light comes on and the rear wheels stop steering, which changes how the car turns.
issues.why: The 4WS system relies on several sensors and its own computer, which can fail with age.
issues.next: Have the 4WS codes read. Used parts are often the only option because new parts are scarce.
